test_title: PYST 9: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: What is "doping" in sports ?

options.text: The use of advanced training techniques to enhance performance.
The consumption of nutritional supplements to improve health
The use of banned substances or methods to unfairly enhance athletic performance.
The practice of psychological conditioning for athletes.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The use of banned substances or methods to unfairly enhance athletic performance.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Doping in sports** refers to the use of **banned substances** or methods by athletes to gain an **unfair advantage** over competitors. The substances used can enhance performance by increasing strength, endurance, or recovery speed.
 
• The practice is considered unethical and is **strictly prohibited** by various sports organizations, including the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA).**
 
• Doping can involve the use of **performance-enhancing drugs** (PEDs) such as anabolic steroids, erythropoietin (EPO), or human growth hormones. These substances can boost muscle mass, oxygen delivery, or overall stamina. *Hence, this aligns with the given correct answer.*
 
• Methods like **blood doping** (injecting oxygenated blood into the body) or the use of masking agents to hide drug use also constitute doping. These practices are banned as they violate the principles of **fair play**.
 
• Athletes caught doping may face **severe consequences**, including suspension, disqualification, or permanent bans from their sport. *Thus, the definition of doping matches the correct option provided.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Categories of banned substances:**

 
 
• **Anabolic agents:** These include anabolic steroids that promote muscle growth. Examples are **testosterone** and nandrolone.
 
• **Stimulants:** Substances like amphetamines or cocaine that enhance alertness and reduce fatigue.
 
• **Hormones:** These include erythropoietin (EPO), human growth hormone (HGH), and insulin, which are used to improve oxygen delivery or muscle repair.
 
 
 
• **Anti-doping regulations and organizations:**
 
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**, established in **1999**, is a global organization that oversees anti-doping efforts. It publishes an annual **Prohibited List** of substances and methods.
 
• National Anti-Doping Organizations (NADOs) in individual countries ensure compliance with global anti-doping standards. For instance, **NADA** (National Anti-Doping Agency) operates in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of doping:**
 
 
• Doping undermines the spirit of sportsmanship by providing an unfair advantage to athletes who use banned substances or methods.
 
• It can have **serious health consequences**, including cardiovascular issues, liver damage, hormonal imbalances, and even death in extreme cases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of high-profile doping cases:**

 
 
• **Lance Armstrong:** The cyclist was stripped of his **seven Tour de France titles** after admitting to using performance-enhancing drugs.
 
• **Maria Sharapova:** The tennis player received a **two-year ban** after testing positive for meldonium, a banned substance, in **2016**.
 
 
 
• **Efforts to combat doping:**
 
 
• Regular testing of athletes is conducted during and outside competition to detect banned substances.
 
• Educational programs are run by organizations like WADA and national bodies to inform athletes about the **risks and consequences of doping**.
 
• Advances in technology, such as biological passports, help track long-term changes in an athlete’s physiology to detect doping.
